clue.text: It is even palindromic

indicators.note: palindromic says the word wanted reads the same from either end, so the answer itself is the wordplay

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A remark that something is flat and balanced, with a nod to wordplay.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue says the answer, meaning 'even', is palindromic: it reads the same forwards and backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A level surface is flat and smooth, which is one sense of even.

clue.text: Fashionably named?

parts.note: read as 'given a name' (one sense of the verb style) and also as 'shaped in a fashionable way', as hair can be

explanation.surface: A query about whether something was given a trendy name.
explanation.walkthrough: To style someone is to call them by a title, and styled hair is fashionably cut, so the question mark flags both readings.
explanation.definitionFit: To style is both to give a title and to design in a fashion, so the word covers both senses.

clue.text: Mean sailor upset students' game

parts.note: mean in the sense of low or contemptible is base

indicators.note: in a down clue upset turns the sailor's letters upside down, so they read bottom to top

parts.note: AB, able seaman, is the usual crossword sailor
L is the learner plate, so two students give LL

explanation.surface: A nasty sailor knocks over the students' ball game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' reverses AB to BA; LL is two learners, L being the learner driver's plate.
explanation.definitionFit: Baseball is an American bat-and-ball sport, an example of a game.

clue.text: Clasp is loose on the Spanish knife

indicators.note: letters that are loose come apart and can be put back in another order

parts.note: el is the Spanish word for the

explanation.surface: A fastening has come undone on a blade from Spain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is loose' shuffles CLASP into SCALP, and EL (Spanish for 'the') is added after it.
explanation.definitionFit: A scalpel is a small sharp surgeon's blade, a kind of knife.

clue.text: Bottom gear

parts.note: not the lowest gear of a car but clothing worn on one's bottom

explanation.surface: A driver changing down to first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bottom gear' sounds like motoring, but gear here is clothes and the bottom is the body part.
explanation.definitionFit: Underpants for the backside are clothing worn on the rear, as the phrase puns.

clue.text: What holidaymakers may assume could be coast erosion

definitions.meaning: clothes that people on holiday put on, assume meaning don
read as two words, the wearing away of the shore

explanation.surface: Tourists might suppose the shoreline is washing away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assume' means put on clothes, not suppose; split the answer and it is a shore being worn down.
explanation.definitionFit: Swimsuits and sandals are garments for the seaside; split into two words it means the shore getting worn down.

clue.text: Check mate in sporting event

parts.note: to check something is to test it
a mate is a partner or equal, a match

explanation.surface: A chess checkmate happens during a sports fixture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Check mate' looks like chess, but each word supplies its own synonym. A TEST MATCH is an international cricket or rugby fixture.
explanation.definitionFit: A Test match is an international fixture in cricket or rugby, a sporting contest.

clue.text: Old car doesn't start, causing exasperation

indicators.note: a word that doesn't start loses its opening letter

parts.note: a banger is British slang for a battered old car

explanation.surface: A clapped-out car won't start, and its owner is fuming.
explanation.walkthrough: BANGER is British slang for an old, unreliable car; 'doesn't start' removes its first letter B.
explanation.definitionFit: Exasperation is irritated fury, which is what anger means.

clue.text: Market's worst seller

parts.note: evokes the idiom about goods nobody will buy being a glut on the market, as well as a dealer in narcotics

explanation.surface: The trader who shifts least stock at the market.
explanation.walkthrough: A 'drug on the market' is something that cannot be sold; the worst kind of seller might also be a pusher.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom 'a drug on the market' names an unsellable product.

clue.text: Spring after spring, it never fails to surprise me

definitions.text: it never fails to surprise me

indicators.note: after places one spring next to the other in sequence

parts.note: a spring of water is a well
a second spring, again a well

explanation.surface: Season after season, someone is perpetually astonished.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spring' tempts as the season, but here it is a water source, a well, twice over.
explanation.definitionFit: The doubled exclamation expresses mild astonishment, the reaction the speaker always has.

clue.text: Decoration with gold backing two firms are after

indicators.note: are after puts the firms behind the gold in the answer
backing means the gold's letters go in reverse order

parts.note: or is the heraldic word for gold
CO is short for company, a firm
the second company, again CO

explanation.surface: Ornamentation with gilt support that a pair of businesses are pursuing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backing' reverses OR (heraldic gold) to RO; two COs (companies) then follow.
explanation.definitionFit: Rococo is an ornate 18th-century style of ornament, so it means elaborate decoration.

clue.text: A letter less than perfect in conception

indicators.note: says the word for perfect is short by one letter at its end

parts.note: perfect means ideal

explanation.surface: Something almost flawless at the moment of creation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A letter less than' trims one letter, the final L, from IDEAL.
explanation.definitionFit: A conception is a notion or thought formed in the mind.

clue.text: Two birds of prey make one

parts.note: an eagle is a bird of prey
an owl is another bird of prey

explanation.surface: A pair of hunting birds combine into a single bird.
explanation.walkthrough: The two raptors joined name a third: the large horned owl of Europe and Asia, which 'one' stands for.
explanation.definitionFit: 'One' stands for a bird of prey, and this large horned species is exactly that.

clue.text: Public announcement of clear round

parts.note: manifest means obvious or clear
O is round in shape

explanation.surface: A statement made about a fault-free show-jumping round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'clear round' suggests show-jumping, but it is MANIFEST plus O, the round letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A manifesto is a published declaration of a party's aims, a public statement.

clue.text: Golf score can make a good story

parts.note: par is the standard score for a golf hole
to be able is to be capable, can

explanation.surface: Golfers bragging about their scores tell a fine yarn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can' is the verb meaning be capable, giving ABLE.
explanation.definitionFit: A parable is a short moral tale, a good story in the sense of one with a lesson.

clue.text: If I react strangely it may be a trick!

indicators.note: strangely says the letters of these words are arranged oddly

explanation.surface: Someone suspects their odd reaction might be a ruse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strangely' rearranges the eight letters of IF I REACT.
explanation.definitionFit: Artifice is cunning deception, a trick or ruse.

clue.text: Workers spread polish

parts.note: worker bees are the classic crossword workers
to wax is to grow or spread

explanation.surface: Labourers apply polish with a cloth.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Workers' are the bees of a hive; to wax is to grow, as the moon does.
explanation.definitionFit: This product made from honeycomb is used to shine furniture and floors.

clue.text: Greene is about to liven things up

indicators.note: about signals the letters are turned around and rearranged

explanation.surface: Graham Greene is set to bring some life to proceedings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' rearranges GREENE IS; Greene looks like the novelist but is just fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: To energise is to fill with vigour, enlivening a situation.

clue.text: Fractions of the highest order

indicators.note: order is the instruction to put the letters into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Portions of the most supreme kind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of the highest order' reads as top-quality, but 'order' rearranges HIGHEST.
explanation.definitionFit: A one-eighth share is a fraction, so these are fractions.

clue.text: Experts visit our organisation

indicators.note: organisation means the letters are put into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Specialists come to inspect the company.
explanation.walkthrough: 'organisation' looks like a company but rearranges VISIT OUR.
explanation.definitionFit: Virtuosi are highly skilled performers, masters of their craft.

clue.text: Food of love at first sight

parts.note: love is nil in tennis, the letter O

indicators.note: first takes just the opening letter of the following word

explanation.surface: Romantic nourishment, falling for someone instantly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'love at first sight' splits into O (love as zero), AT, and S, the first of 'sight'.
explanation.definitionFit: Grain eaten as porridge is a food for people and horses.

clue.text: They may be pierced or just pricked

definitions.text: They may be pierced or just pricked

parts.words: They may be pierced or just pricked
parts.note: body parts that take earrings, or that an alert listener or animal pricks up

explanation.surface: Things punctured by a needle.
explanation.walkthrough: One pierces them for jewellery, and pricks them up to listen.
explanation.definitionFit: The organs of hearing are what get pierced for rings or pricked up when listening.

clue.text: Keep your thanks in check

indicators.note: in places the thanks inside the check

parts.note: to rein is to check or restrain
ta is British informal for thank you

explanation.surface: Restrain your gratitude.
explanation.walkthrough: TA is British informal 'thanks'; 'in' puts it inside REIN.
explanation.definitionFit: To retain something is to hold on to it.

clue.text: Project that is captivating politician supported by left

indicators.note: in a down clue being supported by means having the next piece below
captivating means holding prisoner, so one piece is enclosed by the other

parts.note: MP, Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A scheme that charms a politician and is backed by the left wing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'captivating' puts MP inside IE; 'supported by' sets L beneath it in this down clue. 'Project' is the verb, to propel.
explanation.definitionFit: To project is to throw forward, the same as to drive onward.

clue.text: Observe attack and think it right

parts.note: to observe is to see
a fit is a sudden attack, as of coughing

explanation.surface: Watch an assault and judge it justified.
explanation.walkthrough: 'attack' is a noun, a fit of illness.
explanation.definitionFit: To deem an action appropriate is to judge it proper.

clue.text: Drunk given prison sentence none too soon

parts.note: high means intoxicated
time is slang for a jail term, as in doing time

explanation.surface: A drunk gets jail, and not before time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'time' is a prison term, as in 'doing time'.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying it is about time means something is overdue, happening at last.

clue.text: Cheat with cards and make a pile

explanation.surface: A card sharp cheats and makes a fortune.
explanation.walkthrough: To 'stack the deck' is to rig it; 'make a pile' also tempts as getting rich.
explanation.definitionFit: To rig a deck is to arrange it unfairly, and to heap things is to pile them up.

clue.text: It's possibly hunted out and punished

indicators.note: out here means the chasing goes on the outside, surrounding the other letters

parts.note: hunted means chased

indicators.note: possibly says the letters may be in some other order

explanation.surface: Something was perhaps pursued from cover and penalised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'possibly' shuffles IT'S to TIS, and 'out' puts CHASED outside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To be chastised is to be rebuked or disciplined.
